gm_text: Rain splashes over soot-dark stone as frayed banners flutter above the eastern gate of Cinderwatch, their once-vibrant colors dulled by ash and damp. Mud churns beneath a squeezed line of refugees and wagons, pressed tightly against the guards who maintain a strict choke. Nearby, a tavern runner calls out offers of hot stew and whispers of paid rumors, her voice a sharp contrast to the steady tension in the air. Along the crowded approach, a threadbare watcher stands motionless, eyes darting more to the faces and packs of those waiting than to the gate itself. Just beyond, a notice board catches your eye, its fresh postings listing new taxes and curfew rules, and most grimly, a warning about a missing patrol. A well-appointed townhouse, bearing noble colors, overlooks the muddy square with quiet detachment. The crowd’s murmur, the splatter of rain, and the watchful presence of guards mark the gate district as a place gripped by unease and watchful eyes.
